title: Same-batch $ref dataflow boundary: the dependent sink is gated on the ledger as it stood at batch-evaluation time (no provenance rule fires), and the $ref substitution passes the read's raw result object, which the sink's string input schema rejects — so the sink never executes
note: R08 (boundary leg, ceiling assertion; expectation frozen from the observed artifact behavior of the first 2026-10-08 run, after the source-derived guess (send executes) was refuted). Two mechanisms compose here. (1) Gate timing: policy decisions for a batch are evaluated BEFORE the batch dispatches, so the sink's gate sees an empty ledger — no deny rule fires. (2) Dataflow typing: the DAG's $ref substitution passes the read's whole result object, send_report's string input schema rejects it at dispatch (tool_result error, code execution_error) and the sink never executes. Net effect on this fixture: no leak and no effect — but the reason is schema typing, NOT taint policy, and a sink whose schema accepted objects would not be so spared. The honest guidance stands: run-level threading protects sink calls submitted in steps after the producing step (S1/S2); same-batch $ref dataflow is outside that protection and must not be relied on. A provenance deny here would mean per-dependency evaluation exists — the assertion would then need re-derivation, not silent relaxation.
